label: input w at original position >= 4
explanation: Token-specific feature: fires when the input token is the letter w during the original (pre-<DEL>) phase. It is silent at positions 0-2. At position 3 it fires only weakly (about 0.01-0.05 of max, 0.6% of mass), and from position 4 on it fires every time (precision 1.0 on dev). Magnitude rises with position and as <DEL> gets closer: the largest activations (~3.5) are w as the last original token of L=9 sequences. A second w in a sequence fires more weakly than the first (in_first=0 holds 18% of mass). Never fires on the delimiter or in the copy phase, including when w is fed back or output, and essentially never on any other input token.

issues: The core label and predicate hold up. Test split: precision 1.000, recall 0.875, F1 0.933, mass recall 0.994, and 0 false positives. The feature is silent in the delimiter and copy phases and at t=0-2. Its firing on tokens other than w is scattered noise (about 12 steps in the dev split). All misses are the weak w at t=3 (about 0.02-0.05 of max, 0.6% of mass). Coverage by quartile is 0.50/1/1/1, so only the bottom quartile is missed.

The claim 'magnitude rises ... as <DEL> gets closer' is false; magnitude depends only on absolute position t. Mean activation is mass_recall/recall at fixed t. At t=6: to_go=0 gives 1.487 and to_go=2 gives 1.488. At t=4: to_go=0 gives 0.573 and to_go=3 gives 0.575. The largest values come from w at t=8. That position only exists as the last token of L=9 sequences, so 'closeness to <DEL>' is a confound of position.

The claim 'a second w in a sequence fires more weakly than the first' is false once position is held fixed. At t=6: in_first==1 gives a mean ratio of 1.489 and in_first==0 gives 1.484, essentially identical. In the profile examples a repeated w often fires more strongly ('3 p f u [w:0.29] [w:0.54]'), because the repeat sits at a later position.

Minor: the t=3 activations are small but they happen every time (5877 fires out of about 500000/30 w's at t=3, i.e. near 100% of w's there). So the feature fires on w at t>=3 with a strongly rising magnitude, not a sharp cutoff at t=4. The predicate's t>=4 choice is a reasonable F1 tradeoff, but the label's '>= 4' is a threshold artifact.
skeptic.revised_label: input w in the original phase at position >= 4 (weak at t=3); magnitude grows with absolute position t, not with distance to <DEL> or with repeat count

final_label: input w in the original phase at position >= 4 (weak at t=3); magnitude grows with absolute position t, not with distance to <DEL> or with repeat count
